evidence_chain.link: The presence of unilateral purulent nasal discharge is a key symptom of bacterial sinusitis.
Anatomical obstruction of the nasal cavity may cause unilateral symptoms, but the presence of purulent discharge is more indicative of an infectious process.

ranked_facts.why: The presence of unilateral purulent nasal discharge mixed with blood is more consistent with bacterial sinusitis (B1) than with anatomical obstruction of the nasal cavity (B2).

evidence_chain.link: Bacterial sinusitis often presents with unilateral symptoms.
Allergic rhinitis typically presents with bilateral symptoms.

ranked_facts.why: The unilaterality of symptoms is consistent with bacterial sinusitis (B1), but not with inflammatory processes such as allergic rhinitis (B3).
